metadata.title: Consensus and Chips: From Cyclicals to AI — David with Teacher Xiao X
metadata.guest_role: Buy-side ETF / active-book researcher; ex-futures and sell-side macro

conclusion: David brings Xiao X back from E174. Gold crashed $5,600 to $4,400 in days; silver tagged $1,200 then lost 1.3 in a week. Jan–Jun 2026 is two planets: AI versus everything. Nine of ten daily top reads are AI; the crowded global top-50 is ~90% AI. Aluminum still fell 30–40%. Same frame — more bids than offers, thin chips. Cyclicals peaked into February; AI took the bid. After a mid-year unwind he still says the industry is there. A value PM rarely rotates this fast; a strategist does.
background: E201, taped Aug 13, published Sept 27. E174 (Feb 3) was consensus-and-chips on metals and chemicals during Venezuela/Iran/US headlines. Xiao X: black futures, then steel/coal, sell-side macro, now buy-side ETF and active-book research. He is a 实战派 listener. David wants long-horizon PMs to steal the permission to rotate, not Xiao X's last ticker.
important_facts: E174 print: gold $5,600 to $4,400 in two or three days; silver up to $1,200 then −1.3 in a week — 'largest single-day drop' in the press. Limit-up/limit-down in the same window. Xiao X's consensus-and-chips frame on colored metals, precious, steel, chemicals was the hit. Cyclicals then went sideways to weak from February into June–July. David watched that and found Xiao X's attention had already moved.

AI as the same tape: Jan–Jun 2026 AI versus non-AI is not a factor spread, it is two planets. Top-ten articles 9/10 AI; ~90% of a global top-50 crowded list. Aluminum names −30% to −40% in the same months. Price rises when bids beat offers and the chip pile at that level is thin — K-line first, story second. Cyclicals were strong, then dumped after February; AI inherited the bid. A mid-year unwind inside AI (some names down hard, index still printing 5% days on the chain) does not, for him, kill the industry. A 5% day on the AI chain next to a 30–40% aluminum hole is the two-planet picture in one week.

Who can rotate: David says a long-horizon value PM does not usually jump from copper to GPUs; a strategist does. Xiao X's move is the object. Style years he name-checks (62, 63, 66, 67, 89) are the 'this has happened' list, not a model. May–June consumption/investment notes sit next to the AI cluster. Diligence the bid and the chip depth, not the sector label. OpenAI is the narrative pole; Zhongji (300308.SZ) is the named optical-module way to hold the same bid in A-shares. Steal the permission to rotate when the bid moves, not Xiao X's last ticker.

mental_model.name: Consensus × Chip Depth × Label-Free Bid
mental_model.components: The same frame on gold $5,600→$4,400 and on AI 9/10 headlines. More bids than offers, thin chips, price goes. Sector is a costume. Jan–Jun 2026 two-planet split is the print. A strategist can rotate; a value PM usually cannot. Mid-year AI unwind is weather if the industry bid is still there. 30–40% aluminum drawdowns are the other planet. Keep the method weekly: name the bid and the chip depth, then pick the costume. Nine of ten articles agreeing is a crowded tape, not a free option. Aluminum down 30–40% is what the other planet looks like when the bid leaves.
mental_model.application: NVDA is the global bid pole. 300308.SZ is an A-share optical way to sit in the same crowded 90%. OpenAI is the story, not the chip pile. Do not buy aluminum because E174 was good, and do not buy every AI name because nine of ten articles agree.

key_insights.question: Why can cyclicals become AI?
key_insights.answer: Bids versus offers and chip depth. Gold $5,600→$4,400 and AI 9/10 headlines are one method.

key_insights.question: How split was it?
key_insights.answer: AI versus everything. Aluminum −30–40%. Global crowded top-50 ~90% AI.

key_insights.view: Strategists rotate; value PMs usually don't.
key_insights.question: What should a 实战派 listener copy?
key_insights.answer: The permission to move when the bid moves — not a new valuation religion.
